result.is_trade_type_variant:
Both — and the split is the answer, so neither a blanket "trade-type variant, no key" nor a blanket "seven new families" is right.

TAS is a trade type in CME's own words. cmegroup.com/trading/trading-at-settlement.html: "TAS is an order type that allows you to execute at a spread to the settlement price at any time during the trading session." CME Clearing's TAS/TAM/BTIC note: "Firms will never have positions in the TAS or TAM trading symbols, and need not set these up in their bookkeeping systems." So at the clearing/product level a TAS trade is a WTI position, not a separate product.

But the trade type is carried by a SEPARATE Globex instrument in its OWN security group, and — decisively for this crate — its published session is NOT the underlying's. Every one of my seven shapes closes earlier than its underlying:
- grain TAS 13:15 CT vs globex_grains 13:20 CT (grains.rs CBOT_REGULAR_CURRENT)
- livestock TAS 13:00 CT vs globex_livestock 13:05 CT (livestock.rs REGULAR_CURRENT)
- crude/refined and nat-gas TAS 13:30 CT vs globex_energy 16:00 CT (energy_metals.rs ENERGY_METALS_EXTENDED_CURRENT 17:00–16:00)
- Dutch-gas TAS 10:05 CT and gasoil TAS 10:30 CT, while their underlyings TTF (78:FD) and 7F (80:OP) both sit inside the 1,146-root 17:00–16:00 CT signature
- crypto TAS trade-date roll 15:00 CT vs globex_cryptocurrency 16:00–16:02 CT (cryptocurrency.rs CURRENT_EXTENDED, CME filing 26-114)

The second trap fires here and must be stated plainly: every one of those TAS closes is exactly the END OF THE DAILY SETTLEMENT DETERMINATION RANGE for that asset class, per CME's own "Daily Settlement Time Details" (Livestock 12:59:30-13:00:00 CT; Grains/Oilseeds 13:14:00-13:15:00 CT; Energy Products 14:28:00-14:30:00 ET = 13:30 CT; Bitcoin 14:59:00-15:00:00 CT). So the times I see in the schedule feed are settlement instants — the question is whether CME ALSO publishes them as a session boundary for the TAS book. For three shapes it does; for four it does not, on what I retrieved.

Repo law already half-decided this: futures_profile.rs excludes TAS from GlobexEnergy ("Excludes TAS/TAM/BTIC"), GlobexFx ("excludes eFix, BTIC, TAS"), GlobexLivestock ("excludes options and separately specified TAS sessions") and GlobexRoughRice ("separately specified session types such as TAS and BTIC"), and verification.md repeats it for globex_energy, globex_fx, comex and nymex. No existing key claims TAS. Nothing in the 29 roots can be mapped to an existing key.

RETRIEVAL NOTE FIRST, because it bounds everything below: www.cmegroup.com returns HTTP 403 from this IP on EVERY path — HTML pages, /CmeWS/mvc/ContractSpecs/List, /services/trading-hours-by-product and /confluence/ alike — with the body "This IP address is blocked due to suspected web scraping activity associated with it on this CMEgroup.com page." The full browser header set does not help. So the Session API and the Spec API were unreachable for this whole task; everything below came from web.archive.org id_ snapshots of cmegroup.com, or from cmegroupclientsite.atlassian.net (CME's own Client Systems Wiki), which serves normally and is public and unauthenticated.

1) TAS IS AN ORDER TYPE — CME's landing page, https://web.archive.org/web/20260613215647id_/https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/trading-at-settlement.html
"TAS is an order type that allows you to execute at a spread to the settlement price at any time during the trading session."
"Execute at any point of the trading day rather than waiting for the market close"

2) TAS IS A SEPARATE GLOBEX SYMBOL, NOT A SEPARATE POSITION — CME Clearing, "Trade at Settlement, Trade at Marker, and Basis Trade Index Close", Updated January 25, 2016, https://web.archive.org/web/20190921222524id_/http://www.cmegroup.com/clearing/files/tas-tam-btic.pdf
"On CME Globex, a separate trading symbol is used to distinguish these: normal crude oil trades are in symbol CL, TAS trades are in symbol CLT, and TAM trades are in symbol CLL."
"The TAS trades – in symbol CLT – are done at a differential from the end of day settlement price in the crude oil future, and the TAM trades – in symbol CLL – are done at a differential from the 4:30pm London market closing price."
"Firms will never have positions in the TAS or TAM trading symbols, and need not set these up in their bookkeeping systems."

3) CME SAYS TAS HAS ITS OWN TIME PERIODS BUT DOES NOT STATE THEM — Market Regulation Advisory Notice RA2302-5, Advisory Date July 13, 2023, Effective Date July 31, 2023, https://web.archive.org/web/20251020113006id_/https://www.cmegroup.com/rulebook/files/cme-group-Rule-524.pdf
"Rule 524 permits the initiation of TAS, TAM, BTIC, TACO, and TMAC orders into CME Globex only subsequent to the beginning of each group's pre-open state and during the time period the applicable contracts are available for TAS, TAM, BTIC, TACO, or TMAC trading on CME Globex, as applicable."
NYMEX/COMEX Rule 524: "The Exchange shall determine the products, contract months and time periods during which TAS and TAM transactions shall be permitted."

4) TAS GROUPS HAVE THEIR OWN QUEUE TIMES — CME Client Systems Wiki, "Trade at Settlement - TAS", page 457223974, v2 2025-01-13, https://cmegroupclientsite.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/EPICSANDBOX/pages/457223974/Trade+at+Settlement+-+TAS
"the timing of each TAS groups' pre-open state is randomized. The market state sequence for TAS groups has a market pause ... at 16:00:00 on Sunday and 16:45:00 Monday through Thursday. TAS groups then go into pre-open on Sundays between 16:00:00 and 16:01:00 Central time (CT), and Mondays through Thursdays between 16:45:00 and 16:46:00 CT."
This matches the schedule-file Pre-Opens on all six non-crypto shapes exactly.

5) GRAIN AND LIVESTOCK TAS HOURS — CME fact card "Trading at Settlement (TAS) for Agricultural Futures", PDF created 2023-10-03, linked as current from the 2026-04-20 capture of /trading/agricultural/fact-card-tas-for-agricultural-futures.html; https://web.archive.org/web/20231118234338id_/https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/agricultural/files/fact-card-tas-for-agricultural-futures.pdf
Column heading: "TAS TRADING HOURS"
"GRAINS & OILSEEDS | Corn TAS (ZCT) / Soybean TAS (SBT) / Soybean Oil TAS (ZLT) / Soybean Meal TAS (ZMT) / Chicago Wheat TAS (ZWT) / KC Wheat TAS (KET) | Sunday – Friday, 7:00 p.m. – 7:45 a.m. CT   Monday – Friday, 8:30 a.m. – 1:15 p.m. CT"
"LIVESTOCK | Live Cattle TAS (LET) / Feeder Cattle TAS (GFT) / Lean Hogs TAS (HET) | Monday – Friday 8:30 a.m. – 1:00 p.m. CT"
Also: "TAS order entry is not allowed prior to the beginning of each group's pre-open state, just like other order types".

6) EARLIER EDITIONS OF THE SAME FACT CARD — dated history
PDF created 2015-06-11, https://web.archive.org/web/20150616064756id_/https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/agricultural/files/fact-card-tas-for-agricultural-futures.pdf — grains identical ("Sunday – Friday, 7:00 p.m. – 7:45 a.m. CT / Monday – Friday, 8:30 a.m. – 1:15 p.m. CT"); livestock DIFFERENT: "Monday, 9:05 a.m. – 1 p.m." and "Tuesday – Friday, 8 a.m. – 1 p.m."
PDF created 2016-03-04, https://web.archive.org/web/20200608032955id_/https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/agricultural/files/fact-card-tas-for-agricultural-futures.pdf — livestock already "8:30 a.m. – 1:00 p.m. CT".

7) THE GRAIN DIVERGENCE DATE CANDIDATE — SER-7395R, Notice Date 17 June 2015, Effective Date 05 July 2015, https://web.archive.org/web/20191114001645id_/https://www.cmegroup.com/tools-information/lookups/advisories/ser/SER-7395R.html
"Effective on Sunday, July 5, 2015, for trade date Monday, July 6, 2015 ... CBOT will amend the CME Globex trading hours for non-expiring grain and oilseed futures and all grain and oilseed options"
Current column: "Sunday – Friday, 7:00 p.m. – 7:45 a.m. CT and Monday – Friday, 8:30 a.m. – 1:15 p.m. CT"; new column: "... Monday – Friday, 8:30 a.m. – 1:20 p.m. CT". Appendix 1 (the affected-product list) is referenced but its PDF is not archived at any URL I tried.

8) THE SETTLEMENT-INSTANT TRAP, QUANTIFIED — CME Client Systems Wiki, "Daily Settlement Time Details", page 457085528, v3 2025-01-03, https://cmegroupclientsite.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/EPICSANDBOX/pages/457085528/Daily+Settlement+Time+Details
"Livestock | 12:59:30-13:00:00 CT"; "Grains/Oilseeds | 13:14:00-13:15:00 CT"; "Energy Products | 14:28:00-14:30:00 ET"; "Bitcoin | 14:59:00-15:00:00 CT".
Every TAS close in my seven shapes lands on the END of its class's range.

9) CRYPTO TAS HAS ITS OWN PUBLISHED SCHEDULE — CME Client Systems Wiki, "Cryptocurrency Futures and Options Migration to 24-7 Trading", page 1283194884, v46 2026-08-14, https://cmegroupclientsite.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/EPICSANDBOX/pages/1283194884/Cryptocurrency+Futures+and+Options+Migration+to+24-7+Trading

"Monday through Friday | Daily Maintenance Window (with Trade Date roll) | Close: 3:00:00 p.m. to 3:01:00 p.m. CT  Pause: 3:01:00 p.m. to 3:01:30 p.m. CT | Pause: 3:01:00 p.m. to 3:01:30 p.m. CT  Pre-open: 3:01:30 p.m. to 3:04:30 p.m. CT  No cancel: 3:04:30 p.m. to 3:05:00 p.m. CT  Open: 3:05:00 p.m. to 4:01:00 p.m. CT  Pause: 4:01:00 p.m. to 4:02:00 p.m. CT  Open: 4:02:00 p.m. CT"

Separate table "Future Cryptocurrency Futures and Options Schedule" (the futures/options books): "Monday through Friday | Daily Maintenance Window (with Trade Date roll) | Close: 4:00:00 p.m. to 4:01:00 p.m. CT | ... Open: 4:02:00 p.m. CT" — a different roll time from the TAS table.
Corroborated by https://web.archive.org/web/20260610025555id_/https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/cryptocurrencies/tas-on-cryptocurrency-futures.html: "Globex 24/7 with the exception of the following maintenance windows: Saturday: 2:00 a.m. to 4:00 a.m. CT  Monday - Friday: 3:00 p.m. to 3:05 p.m. CT".

CME filing 26-114 (05/13/26, "Expansion of the Trading and Clearing Hours for all Cryptocurrency Futures and Options on Futures Contracts", effective Friday, May 29, 2026), https://web.archive.org/web/20260823053410id_/https://www.cmegroup.com/content/dam/cmegroup/market-regulation/rule-filings/2026/5/26-114.pdf, Table 2 expanded Globex column: "24/7 with the exception of the following maintenance windows: Saturday 2:00 a.m. to 4:00 a.m. CT. FOR THE THREE NEW-KEY CANDIDATES (17 roots):
1. Regular-vs-extended classification. No TAS document CME publishes states it, for any of the seven shapes. The ag fact card gives times under "TAS TRADING HOURS" and stops. Repo law requires the classification before a profile ships, so even the best-sourced shapes cannot be coded from what I have. The likely route is CME's Daily Bulletin RTH/ETH convention, as the weather row used.
2. Grain TAS: Appendix 1 of SER-7395R. It is the one document that would turn the 2015-07-05 grains 13:15->13:20 move into a sourced NON-event for the TAS books. Not archived at /tools-information/lookups/advisories/ser/SER-7395R.pdf, /rulebook/files/SER-7395R.pdf, or /content/dam/cmegroup/notices/ser/2015/06/SER-7395R.pdf. Try the CFTC copy of the corresponding CBOT 40.6(a) certification instead — cftc.gov is reachable from here.
3. Livestock TAS: the effective day of the "Monday 9:05 / Tue-Fri 8:00" -> "Mon-Fri 8:30" change. Bracketed 2015-06-11..2016-03-04 by two fact-card creation dates only. A bracket is not a date; SER-7591 (the underlying's 2016-02-29 move, already in the repo) is the obvious place to look for whether it also names the TAS codes.
4. Crypto TAS: the filing that moved TBT/TBM/TET/TEM/TSL/TMS/TXP/TMX to the 24/7 TAS schedule. 26-114 does not name them. Also the 2023 BTC/MBT launch, the 2025 ETH/MET and SOL/XRP additions (CME news pages exist), and the pre-2026 grid.
5. Crypto TAS side-finding that also touches the EXISTING globex_cryptocurrency row: in the 2026-08-30 schedule file, Saturday 2026-08-29 runs 02:00 CT close -> 05:45 CT Pre-Open -> 06:00 CT open for both the futures and the TAS groups, against the wiki's and 26-114's 03:45/04:00. Either the Saturday window was extended that week or the published grid moved.

FOR THE FOUR UNRESOLVED ENERGY SHAPES (12 roots):

THE ENVELOPE. The signature decodes (verbatim from market-hours-electronic-envelope-candidates.tsv, row d21acb34…, column full_week_transitions) as: `75=20260831|386=3|336=21|341=20260830210000000000|625=30|336=17|341=20260830220000000000|336=4|341=20260831210000000000|75=20260901|386=3|336=21|341=20260831214500000000|625=30|336=17|341=20260831220000000000|336=4|341=20260901210000000000` — Sunday Pre-Open 21:00 UTC = 16:00 CT, Ready 22:00 UTC = 17:00 CT, Close next day 21:00 UTC = 16:00 CT; weekday Pre-Open 21:45 UTC = 16:45 CT. Five trade dates only, so the weekly close is Friday 16:00 CT. That is byte-for-byte the current `globex_fx` / `globex_energy` / `globex_weather` / `globex_spot_quoted` envelope.

WHY IT MUST SPLIT. The crate already holds THREE mutually incompatible regular/extended classifications on this one envelope, so the envelope cannot select a key:
  (a) extended-only, `regular: &[]` — fx.rs:126, energy_metals.rs:136, weather.rs:301, spot_quoted.rs:178;
  (b) `regular` = MON_FRI 08:30–15:15 CT plus extended — cme_group.rs:93–97 (`CME_REGULAR`), used by `globex_equity_index`;
  (c) `regular` = the whole envelope, no extended/RTH split — cme_nikkei.rs:63, whose module comment states "NKD is a pure-Globex international equity-index contract: it has no pit/RTH split, so its entire envelope is the regular session".
`globex_interest_rates` is also `regular: &[]` (interest_rates.rs:154). The CME TradingSessionList publishes none of this, exactly as the brief warns.

THE FOUR TRADE-TYPE VARIANTS, and the pattern they reveal. Row 1 contains only "+"-flavour (forward) variants; every PLAIN trade type sits in a different row with a different window. That asymmetry is itself sourced:
  • `6EP` (group 88:6X, "BTIC+ on NEARBY EURO CURRENCY"). CME's own FAQ: "BTIC+ contracts can be traded through the standard CME Globex trading hours of Sunday-Friday 5:00 p.m.-4:00 p.m. CT." Its plain sibling 6EB is in inventory row 34 ("EUR BTIC 09:40"), matching the same FAQ's "BTIC can be traded on CME Globex against the current day's reference price up to 3:40 p.m. London time (typically 9:40 a.m. CT)." So 6EP's window IS the underlying's session → NOT a distinct session family. 6EB's is not.
  • `ES1`, `ES2` (group 68:SK) = Nearby / Deferred BTIC+ on E-mini S&P 500; `EQ1` (group 68:4T) = TACO+ on E-mini S&P 500. Confirmed by CME Globex Notice 2019-08-26, whose table reads "Nearby BTIC+ Futures on E-mini Standard & Poor's 500 Stock Price Index Futures ES1 SK 318 / Deferred BTIC+ … ES2 SK 318 / TACO+ Futures on E-mini Standard & Poor's 500 Stock Price Index Futures EQ1 4T 318" — the tag-1151 SecurityGroups SK and 4T match the catalog exactly. Their plain siblings are elsewhere: EST/NQT/RLT (BTIC) in row 2 at 17:00–15:00 and ESQ/NQQ/RTQ (TACO) in row 19 at 08:30, and CME's TACO FAQ states those windows verbatim ("Trading session …terminates at 8:30 a.m. CT / 3:00 p.m. CT", "…begins at 10:00 a.m. CT prior day … / 5:00 p.m. CT on prior day").
  UNLIKE 6EP, I could not retrieve any CME statement of the ES1/ES2/EQ1 session window, and CME Globex Notice 2021-06-21 says of the halt removal "S&P 500 futures and options (250 multiplier) as well as all BTIC and TACO products will not be impacted" — which, if BTIC+/TACO+ count as "BTIC and TACO products", means their halt history diverges from `globex_equity_index`. So ES1/ES2/EQ1 stay unresolved.

Everything else in row 1 (1,142 roots) is an ordinary product, not a trade type. The bucket breaks down as: weather 179, spot-quoted 8, CME FX 50, CME rates (seg 82) 6, CBOT rates (seg 84) 45, CME/CBOT equity index (seg 68) 50, CME/CBOT/MGEX commodity (seg 70 non-weather) 19, NYMEX/COMEX (seg 78/80) 785.

result.is_trade_type_variant:
TRADE-TYPE VARIANTS, all seven shapes — and CME says so in its own words, not by inference. But every one of them ALSO carries a published trading window that ends at the marker instant and is NOT the underlying's close, so "variant" does not mean "reuse the underlying's key" here.

(a) They are variants, not products. Energy TAM FAQ: "TAM is a pricing mechanism for a transaction in the applicable underlying futures contract. Fees, positions limits, and reporting levels are based on what applies to the underlying futures contract." Copper TAM FAQ, under the heading "Is a trade in Copper TAM different to a trade in COMEX Copper Futures?": "No, it is not. Copper TAM transaction allows market participants to trade in the COMEX Copper Futures contract at the London Marker Price, plus or minus the transaction price of the TAM trade. Once the London Marker Price is established, Copper TAM trades are resolved into positions in the COMEX Copper Futures contract." TMAC FAQ: "Once the marker price is established, the price of the underlying futures position will be determined by adding the agreed upon spread to the marker price." TACO page: "For all TACO transactions, once the official opening index level is published, the associated futures are cleared at a price equal to the opening cash index level, plus the agreed upon basis." The TMAC/BTIC comparison guide tabulates them under "DELIVERED POSITION (E-MINI FUTURES)": TACO -> ES, NQ, RTY; TMAC -> ES, NQ, RTY, YM.

(b) But the window is genuinely different, and CME publishes it as a window, not merely as a marker instant. This is the specific trap the brief named, so I checked each shape against a CME sentence that states a SESSION boundary rather than an expiry/settlement instant:
- Energy TAM (CLL/BZL/HOL/RBL, CLS/BZS, CLC): "CLS and BZS trading halts at the marker time, daily, at 4:30 p.m. Singapore time (2:30/3:30 a.m. Central time). CLC trading halts at the marker time, daily, at 3:00 p.m. China time (1:00/2:00 a.m. Central time). CLL, RBL, HOL and BZL trading halts at the marker time, daily, at 4:30 p.m. London time." That is CME stating a daily trading halt of the instrument, coincident with the marker. It matches the TradingSessionList closes exactly (15:30Z / 08:30Z / 07:00Z on 2026-08-31 = 16:30 London BST / 16:30 SGT / 15:00 China).
- TMAC (ESX/NQX/RTX/YMX): a published contract-spec row, "TRADING HOURS — CME Globex: Sunday - Friday 6:00 p.m. - 4:00 p.m. ET", against the E-mini underlying's 6:00 p.m. - 5:00 p.m. ET. Matches the feed close 20:00Z = 16:00 ET exactly. I deliberately did NOT use the adjacent "TERMINATION OF TRADING" row on the same page ("TMAC trading shall terminate at 4:00 P.M. ET on the business day immediately preceding the last trade date for such futures contract") — that is contract expiry, the exact confusion that nearly produced six event-contract families.
- TACO (ESQ/NQQ/RTQ): published contract-spec row, "Trading Hours — 10:00 a.m. CT previous day to 8:30 AM CT / For each trade day, trading starts at 10:00 a.m. CT the previous day." Both endpoints match the feed (ready 15:00Z = 10:00 CT on T-1; close 13:30Z = 08:30 CT on T). 08:30 CT is also the 09:30 ET cash open (the marker), but CME states it as the trading-hours end.
- Gold TAM (GCD) and Copper TAM (HGF): I found NO CME sentence stating a session boundary. All I retrieved is the marker calculation window ("Gold futures PM markers are calculated from trade data from 3:00 p.m. – 3:02 p.m. prevailing London time"; copper "12:34 p.m. – 12:35 p.m. London Time") and, for copper, an order-entry cutoff ("may enter any of the following TAM prices up until 12:34:59 p.m. London time"). The feed closes (14:02Z = 15:02 London; 11:35Z = 12:35 London) line up with the marker instants. Under the brief's rule that is precisely the case where a marker instant must not be read as a daily close, so these two stay unresolved.

(c) Consequence for keying: reuse is barred both by evidence and by the repo's own scoping text. `globex_energy` is documented "Excludes TAS/TAM/BTIC, options, and products whose own specification publishes a different grid"; `globex_equity_index` is documented "Excludes full-size S&P 500 (`SP`), Nikkei 225 Dollar (`NKD`), and BTIC/TACO products". Mapping any of these roots to those keys would report the wrong close by 5.5 hours (TAM London), 12.5 hours (TAM Singapore), 1 hour (TMAC) or 7.5 hours (TACO).

result.strongest_counterargument:
THE STRONGEST COUNTERARGUMENT — the seven shapes are mechanically derived, not seven schedule families, and the group boundary is arbitrary.

Every one of the seven TAS envelopes is exactly {the underlying family's OPEN} + {a CLOSE equal to the end of that asset class's daily settlement determination range}. I re-fetched CME's own "Daily Settlement Time Details" (Client Systems Wiki page 457085528, https://cmegroupclientsite.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/EPICSANDBOX/pages/457085528/Daily+Settlement+Time+Details) and read the whole table, not just the four rows the verdict quoted. It reads verbatim: "Livestock | 12:59:30-13:00:00 CT", "Grains/Oilseeds | 13:14:00-13:15:00 CT", "Bitcoin | 14:59:00-15:00:00 CT", "Energy Products | 14:28:00-14:30:00 ET", and also "Gold | 13:29:00-13:30:00 ET", "Silver | 13:24:00-13:25:00 ET", "Copper | 12:59:00-13:00:00 ET", "Palladium | 12:58:00-13:00:00 ET", "Platinum | 13:03:00-13:05:00 ET", "Treasuries | 13:59:30-14:00:00 CT". Those last six land exactly on inventory rows 15 (gold TAS 12:30), 25 (silver TAS 12:25), 18 (copper TAS 12:00), 38 (palladium TAS 12:00), 33 (platinum TAS 12:05) and 13 (Treasury TAS 14:00) — the same rule, outside this verdict's group. CME's own Treasury TAS FAQ (https://web.archive.org/web/20260312155855id_/https://www.cmegroup.com/articles/faqs/faq-trading-at-settlement-tas-for-us-treasury-futures.html) publishes no hours at all, only "the yet-to-be-determined daily settlement price calculated at 3 p.m. ET" — and 3 p.m. ET is 14:00 CT, row 13's close.

The livestock case proves the derivation rather than merely suggesting it. The verdict's own bracket is the evidence: the 2015-06-11 fact card gives livestock TAS "Monday, 9:05 a.m. – 1 p.m." and "Tuesday – Friday, 8 a.m. – 1 p.m." — the OLD livestock underlying open, with the settlement-anchored 13:00 close; the 2016-03-04 card gives "8:30 a.m. – 1:00 p.m. CT" — the NEW underlying open, same 13:00 close. TAS did not have an independent history; it inherited the open and kept the settlement close. So a reviewer can argue the crate would be minting ~10 keys (rows 9, 10, 11, 13, 15, 18, 21, 22, 25, 28, 33, 37, 38 are all TAS) whose entire content is a formula, and that the honest model is the underlying key plus a per-class settlement instant held by the caller's catalog.

Two things make the group boundary itself look arbitrary, which sharpens this. First, the verdict's group is labelled "energy and agricultural" but contains crypto (row 9) and excludes metals and Treasury TAS, which are the same phenomenon. Second, CME's own taxonomy disagrees with the verdict's split: I opened the "TAS Cycle Guide" workbook behind https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/trade-at-settlement-outright-calendar-spread-availability.html — the file is /trading/files/tas-tam-eligibility.xlsx — and its tabs are exactly "Cryptocurrency TAS / Energy TAS / Grain and Oilseed TAS / Livestock TAS / Metals TAS / Treasury TAS". The single "Energy TAS" sheet, titled "Trading at Settlement (TAS) Outright and Calendar Spread Availability - NYMEX Energy Futures", carries "Light Sweet Crude Oil (CLT)", "Micro Crude Oil (MCT)", "Henry Hub Natural Gas (NGT)", "Last Day Financial (HHT)", " (100mt) Bullet (7FT)", "Month Futures (TAS)" and "Calendar Month Futures (TTS)" — i.e. CME treats rows 10, 22, 28 and 37 as ONE asset-class group, while the verdict treats them as four unresolved families. (The workbook publishes contract months only; it has no hours column, so it corroborates the verdict on that narrow point.)

Why the verdict nevertheless survives THIS objection: the crate answers "is this identity tradeable at instant t". At 14:00 CT a CL holder is trading and a CLT holder is not — the 80:CT group is closed 13:30–16:45 CT and then runs a Pre-Open/Ready cycle, which a settlement or marker instant inside a session would never produce. And the repo has already foreclosed reuse in writing: futures_profile.rs excludes TAS from GlobexEnergy, GlobexFx, GlobexLivestock and GlobexRoughRice, and verification.md repeats it on globex_energy, globex_fx, comex and nymex. So "derived" explains why the divergence exists; it does not remove the need to model it. The decision the parent actually owes is granularity — one energy-TAS key over CME's own "Energy TAS" asset class versus four — and that is a decision the verdict never framed.

result.strongest_counterargument:
THE STRONGEST DEFENCE OF THE VERDICT AGAINST MY ATTACK — stated at full strength, because it is not frivolous.

My whole case rests on one channel: `https://r.jina.ai/` in front of cmegroup.com URLs. Two objections follow, and the second is serious.

(1) CHANNEL QUALITY. A text-extraction reader returns extracted text, not the document's own rendering. The repo already says so in `docs/schedules/sources.md`: quotations obtained this way are "high-confidence but not independently confirmed against the primary rendering". So every quotation below is one grade weaker than a direct retrieval. This does not rescue the verdict, though — it never *tried* the channel, and the repo used it the same day.

(2) THE REAL ONE — IS `trading-hours-by-product` A SCHEDULE SOURCE OR THE ENVELOPE FEED IN A DIFFERENT WRAPPER? My central claim against the verdict's two "cannot determine" rows is that CME publishes `{"marketEventType":"closed","eventTime":"09:02"}` for GCD and `06:35` for HGF. But that service's vocabulary — preopen / open / paused / closed — is the Globex state machine, one-to-one with the TradingSessionList's tag-336 statuses (21 Pre-Open, 17 Ready, 2 Pause, 4 Close). The brief's governing constraint is that CME's electronic-envelope publication seeds a question and cannot close it, because it reports when the book stops matching rather than what the operator says the instrument's session is. On a strict reading that objection transfers intact: `closed@09:02` may be the rendered state transition at the end of the gold PM marker window, and reading it as "the session ends here" is exactly the marker-instant-as-daily-close error the brief warned about — the same error that nearly produced six event-contract families. On that reading the verdict's conservatism on GCD/HGF is correct discipline and my correction is the reckless move.

WHY I STILL THINK IT FAILS, and where it partly succeeds:
- The brief itself distinguishes the two. It names the TradingSessionList as the thing that cannot close a profile, and separately names this API as a retrieval route that "settles queue windows and holidays" — i.e. as a settling source.
- The repo already treats it as citable primary evidence in shipped production code. `src/calendar/schedules/futures/us/spot_quoted.rs` cites `https://www.cmegroup.com/services/trading-hours-by-product?id=11086` and uses it to establish both a holiday split and an envelope divergence against `ES`, "read 2026-09-06" — today.
- It is verifiable where independent prose exists. For the five energy TAM roots the service's `closed` times agree exactly with the FAQ's own words, "CLS and BZS trading halts at the marker time, daily, at 4:30 p.m. Singapore time". A publication that is right everywhere it can be checked is reasonable evidence where prose is absent, especially when CME's own TAS/TAM eligibility table files GCD and HGF in the same document as CLL/CLS/CLC.
- The objection is anyway moot for TACO, where the halt is stated in prose twice, in a dated notice and in the contract specification.

WHERE THE DEFENCE DOES LAND: it correctly limits what I have proved. The service is a *current* snapshot with no history, so GCD's and HGF's daily close is sourced today and not through their dated past — a `Partial` basis, which is normal in this crate, not a `Primary` one. And the defence's second half is unanswerable: even if I am entirely right that all seven shapes are now sourced, the verdict's cross-zone structural blocker means five of them may not be writable as `MarketHoursKey` profiles at all — so promoting GCD and HGF out of "unresolved" moves them into a bucket that is itself blocked. That is why my correction keeps the representability question as the gate and merely reorders the queue behind it.
result.corrected_recommendation:
VERDICT SURVIVES ON THE CLASSIFICATION, FAILS ON THE EVIDENCE. The headline call — trade-type variants that nevertheless carry their own published windows, `roots_to_existing_keys` empty, no reuse of `globex_energy` / `globex_equity_index` — is correct and is now stronger than the verdict made it. But two of seven shapes are in the wrong bucket, most of the "STILL NEEDS SOURCING" items are already sourced, and 6 of the 7 retrieval blockers are false. They are false because the verdict did not try the retrieval channel this repository itself used and documented on the same day.

=== 0. THE CHANNEL THE VERDICT MISSED ===
Direct cmegroup.com is IP-blocked from this network, exactly as the verdict says — I reproduced HTTP 403 "This IP address is blocked due to suspected web scraping activity" on the HTML page, on `/CmeWS/mvc/ContractSpecs/List/productId/8460`, on `/services/trading-hours-by-product` and on `/services/product-slate`. But a public text-extraction reader in front of the same cmegroup.com URLs serves all of them. This is not a new invention: `docs/schedules/sources.md` records it as an accepted (weaker) channel, and `src/calendar/schedules/futures/us/spot_quoted.rs` cites both `https://www.cmegroup.com/services/trading-hours-by-product?id=11086` and `https://www.cmegroup.com/CmeWS/mvc/ContractSpecs/List/productId/11086` in shipped comments, "read 2026-09-06". Everything below came through it.

=== 1. GCD AND HGF ARE NOT "CANNOT DETERMINE" — THIS IS THE BIGGEST ERROR ===
CME's own trading-hours service publishes labelled session events for both, in the same vocabulary and the same publication as the five shapes the verdict accepted:
- GCD (id 8407, group GM): `preopen@16:00`/`open@17:00` Sunday; daily `closed@09:02`; weekday `preopen@16:50`/`open@17:00`.
- HGF (id 8652, group TR): same queue shape; daily `closed@06:35`.
The verdict's stated reason for withholding — "any CME statement that GCD trading halts or closes at that instant" was missing — no longer holds: CME's word for the event is `closed`. Both also have dated launch notices with named security groups:
- GCD — CME Globex Notice 20171016: "Effective this Sunday, October 22 (trade date Monday, October 23), Gold London Trade At Marker First PM will be listed for trading on CME Globex...", table "Gold London Trade At Marker First PM | GCD | GM". Corroborates Clearing advisory 17-356.

Move both into `roots_needing_new_keys` at the same evidence grade as CLC.

=== 2. THE HGF ROUTE-DRIFT BLOCKER IS AN ARTEFACT ===
The verdict deferred HGF partly on the audit's "HGF 78/TR -> 78/HT". BOTH THINGS ARE TRUE AT ONCE, and the resolution is evidence-based, not a guess.

(a) The daily close of every one of my six shapes IS a settlement instant. CME's own "Daily Settlement Time Details" page states the daily settlement determination ranges: Gold "13:29:00-13:30:00 ET", Silver "13:24:00-13:25:00 ET", Platinum "13:03:00-13:05:00 ET", Copper "12:59:00-13:00:00 ET", Palladium "12:58:00-13:00:00 ET", Treasuries "13:59:30-14:00:00 CT". Converted, those end instants are 12:30 / 12:25 / 12:05 / 12:00 / 12:00 CT and 14:00 CT — an exact, six-for-six match to the closes in the schedule file. So the trap the brief warns about is live here: read naively, these are six settlement fixings, not six session closes.

(b) But CME ALSO publishes these as trading sessions in its own hours tables, distinct from the underlying's, and dates changes to them. On CME's metals trading-hours page (captures 2011-10-29 through 2015-03-22) "Gold TAS", "Silver TAS" and "Copper TAS" are their own product rows, with their own Pre-Open and their own "Electronic Trading (Sunday)" / "Electronic Trading (Weekday)" values — 18:00-13:30 / 18:00-13:25 / 18:00-13:00 ET — sitting two rows away from "Gold Futures & Options ... 18:00-17:15 ET". And CME Globex Notice 2016-12-19 changes a TAS product's hours in exactly session language: "the trading hours for the European Low Sulphur Gasoil (100mt) Bullet Futures Trade at Settlement (TAS) cease daily at 11:30 a.m. Eastern time (ET). Currently, the trading session closes daily at 12:00 p.m. ET."

So: TAS is a trade type whose instruments are nonetheless given their own CME Globex security groups (tag 1151) and their own published session window, whose close happens to be defined by the underlying's settlement instant. That is NOT "the underlying's session", and it is NOT the event-contract failure mode (a per-contract expiry misread as a daily close) — the Close state recurs on every trade date for the security group, and CME's rulebook Rule 524 says the Exchange sets "the products, contract months and time periods during which TAS and TAM transactions shall be permitted" and that a TAS-eligible contract has a "prescribed pre-open time period" of its own.

CONSEQUENCE FOR MODELLING: no root in this group may reuse the underlying's key. Mapping GCT to globex_energy or ZNS to globex_interest_rates would report the market tradeable for 2-4 hours a day after TAS trading has closed — an executable-hours error, the class the repo ranks most serious. Both keys already exclude TAS by their documented scope (futures_profile.rs:148 "Excludes TAS/TAM/BTIC"; verification.md globex_energy "TAS/TAM/BTIC, options, and different product clocks are excluded").

Note also that the queue grid is CME-wide-per-trade-type, not per-product: the pause/pre-open sequence is identical across all TAS groups (see evidence item 3), while only the close differs by product. So the family boundary is per-underlying-metal (and per Treasury complex), not per trade type.

=== 1. Rulebook: the Exchange sets TAS time periods and a TAS-specific pre-open ===
NYMEX Rulebook Chapter 5, Rule 524 "TRADING AT SETTLEMENT ("TAS") AND TRADING AT MARKER ("TAM") TRANSACTIONS":
  "The Exchange shall determine the products, contract months and time periods during which TAS and TAM transactions shall be permitted."
  524.A.1: "A TAS order may be entered on Globex at any time the applicable contract is available for TAS trading on Globex and during such TAS-eligible contract's prescribed pre-open time period. The initiation of any TAS order on Globex outside these time periods is prohibited."
https://web.archive.org/web/20231206165437id_/https://www.cmegroup.com/content/dam/cmegroup/rulebook/NYMEX/1/5.pdf
(The Rule 524 TAS/TAM Table the chapter points to is https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/files/tas-tam-eligibility.xlsx — retrieved at https://web.archive.org/web/20260830100729id_/... — and contains sheets "Metals TAS" and "Treasury TAS". It publishes eligible contract months ONLY; a full string sweep of the workbook found no hours anywhere in it.)

The strongest defence of the original verdict — and it is a real one, not a formality — is that the "TAS:" line I found sits *inside the underlying contract's own "Trading Hours" cell*, immediately alongside a "CME ClearPort:" line. This repository has twice ruled that the ClearPort line in exactly that cell is NOT a session: `globex_weather` excludes "CME ClearPort, a clearing-submission window rather than a session", and `globex_spot_quoted` repeats it verbatim. A strict reader can therefore say that this cell enumerates *venue and order-type availability windows for one product complex*, not session boundaries for a distinct security group, and that the "TAS:" line is the same category of statement as the ClearPort line the repo throws away. That reading is reinforced by the fact that the closes it states (13:30/13:25/13:05/13:00 ET) are still numerically identical to CME's published settlement determination end-instants — so a line that merely repeats the settlement instant does not, on its own, disprove the trap the brief warned about; it could be documenting "TAS orders are accepted until the settlement fixing" rather than "the session closes". Finally, even granting my reading, the platinum and palladium evidence runs 2017–2021 and stops: CME's server-rendered specification pages 301 from March 2022 and the modern replacements are client-rendered shells, so a `Primary` claim about *today's* boundaries still rests on the schedule feed, which repo law says only seeds.

Why it still fails. (1) The 2017-08-02 platinum specification does not use availability language, it uses cessation language: "Trading ceases daily at 1:05 PM ET." That is the same construction as the CME Globex Notice of 2016-12-19 which the verdict itself accepted as decisive — "the trading hours for the ... Trade at Settlement (TAS) cease daily at 11:30 a.m. ... Currently, the trading session closes daily at 12:00 p.m. ET." The verdict cannot accept that sentence as proof of a session for Gasoil and reject the identical construction for Platinum. (2) The ClearPort analogy breaks on the facts: ClearPort is a clearing-submission venue with no order book, whereas each TAS product is its own CME Globex security group (tag 1151) with its own order book and its own recurring Close state on every trade date. (3) Decisively, the palladium specification captured 2019-07-17 states the *whole session structure*, not just an end instant: "TAS: Sunday - Friday 5:00 p.m. - 12:00 p.m.(CT) (6:00 p.m. - 1:00 p.m. ET) with a 60-minute break each day beginning at 4:00 p.m.(CT) (5:00 p.m. ET)". An open, a close, and a daily break is a session description; a settlement fixing has no 60-minute break.

> `Trading will terminate at the end of the daily settlement period of the Underlying Futures contract on the named date of the Event Contract.`
> `Example:`
> `ECESG412: Daily Expiring Event Contract on E-min S&P 500 Futures to expire on February 12, 2024`
> `ECESH428: End-of-Quarter Event Contract on E-mini S&P 500 Futures set to expire on March 28, 2024 (last business day of March 2024)`

Still current: the CME event-contract specifications PDF, both the 2026‑01‑04 and 2026‑07‑07 captures, lists for ECES and ECNQ "*1 zero days until expiration (DTE) event contract / 1 event contract expiring on the last business day of Mar, Jun, or Sep / 1 event contract expiring on the last business day of the calendar year*". So at 15:00 CT on a Tuesday, ECES has instruments listed that are not expiring. The root is provably not emptied at T. Advisory 24‑011 nonetheless re-prints the *unchanged* hours cell ("ECES; ECNQ, ERTY; ECYM; ECBTC: Sunday 5:00 p.m.- Friday 3:00 p.m."), which is only coherent if that cell is not a daily-close statement.

## 6. Correction to the catalog reading

The `catalog-artifacts` rows for these roots (`synthetic_no_ready`, groups "SYNTHETIC EOC VES/EQUITY/METALS/CRUDE/NYMEX/ECB", states `2,4`) are **not** the event contracts. CME Client Systems Wiki, "Event Contracts" page (version 2026‑08‑14): "*Additionally, non-tradable underlying futures are listed to support the options*", with a table row "*Non-tradable Synthetic Future … Order Entry Allowed: No*". Those GLBX definitions are the synthetic underlying futures; the tradeable instruments are options (`PFType` = `OOF`, `ProdSubTyp` = `EVENT` per the Event Contracts Master File page). The audit's exclusion of them was right, and they carry no information about this family's session. `market-hours-nontradable-groups.tsv` is consistent with this: ECES sits with `KYP10/11/13/15`, the SPAN synthetic codes for the hourly S&P event contracts named in advisory 25‑326.

## 7. What is actually sourced

Identical in SER‑8968R (2022‑08‑25), Clearing Advisory 22‑355 (2022‑09‑20), SER‑9092 (2023), Clearing Advisory 24‑011 (2024‑01‑10) and every archived activetrader capture through 2025‑09‑16 — **for all eleven roots, with no per-root variation, and never amended**:

- Timezone Central Prevailing Time (America/Chicago).
- `CME Globex Pre Open: Sunday 4:00 – 5:00 p.m. Monday – Thursday 4:45 – 5:00 p.m.`
- Week opens Sunday 5:00 p.m.
- `Next day's Event Contract will list at 5:00 p.m.`
- No Friday-evening reopen (the pre-open row names only Sunday and Monday–Thursday).

Corroborating the 17:00 open independently: CME Client Systems Wiki, "Event Contracts Master File" — "*Files are published every day … between 3:30 p.m. and 4:00 p.m. CT, prior to the opening of trading for the new day on CME Globex at 5:00 p.m. CT.*"

**Not sourced anywhere:** any Monday–Thursday close instant; any RTH/ETH classification; whether the Monday–Thursday 16:45–17:00 queue implies a market-wide close or is only the listing queue for the newly listed next-day contract. The only other statement I found touching a daily close is a hypothetical in CFTC filing 22‑376 — "*Trading in the Event Contract will close at the same time as trading of the ES contract*" — which is illustrative prose, and which points at 16:00 CT (ES's Globex close), not at 15:00. It cuts against T, not for it.

## 8. Defensible modelling

Do **not** encode six profiles keyed to T, and do not encode a Monday–Thursday close at T. On present evidence:

1. **One family, not six.** Every element CME publishes as a *session* — the Sunday 16:00–17:00 CT queue, the Monday–Thursday 16:45–17:00 CT queue, the 17:00 CT open, the absent Friday reopen — is byte-identical across all eleven roots and has never been amended since 2022‑09‑18. The only per-root numbers in the entire evidence base are expirations, and SER‑9624 shows CME does not vary the session by them.
2. **Encode the queue windows and the 17:00 open**; they are primary-sourced on the launch day and re-stated four times since.
3. **The executable close is the gap, and it is an executable-hours gap** — the serious kind under the repo's own priority rule, not a queue-onset gap. Say so explicitly rather than filling it with a termination time.
4. If a close must be encoded to make the rules well-formed, the only honest form is the **sourced intersection**: the window open under every reading, `17:00 → T`, carried with an in-table note that `T` is CME's published end-of-range, that CME's own gloss (advisory 25‑326) calls that end an expiration time, and that the `T → 16:45` interval is of **unknown** state — not sourced-dark. That is a conservative envelope, not a published grid, and it must not be written up as six sourced daily closes. Under the merged-key form the intersection across the ten roots collapses to Friday 12:00 CT (ECHG), which under-reports the equity-index roots by three hours; that cost is the reason to keep ten named profiles that currently coincide (per the "a venue that merely coincides still gets its own named profile" convention) rather than one.
5. **ECBTC still forks at 2026‑05‑29** on product semantics, as the research file argues.

My recommendation: keep the family **blocked for a full grid** and record it as an unmodelled family with the reason stated, or ship option 4 with the caveats in the table comment. What must not ship is the current write-up's claim that the six T values are daily session closes — that claim is now affirmatively contradicted by CME.

## 3. The finding that matters most: variant vs. family

### 3.1 The one general rule that came out of all six groups

Every trade-type instrument surveyed here closes at an instant that is **also** a settlement, marker or fixing instant for its asset class. CME's *"Daily Settlement Time Details"* matches the observed closes six-for-six in the metals/Treasury group and four-for-four in the energy/ag group: Livestock `12:59:30-13:00:00 CT`, Grains/Oilseeds `13:14:00-13:15:00 CT`, Energy `14:28:00-14:30:00 ET`, Bitcoin `14:59:00-15:00:00 CT`, Gold `13:29:00-13:30:00 ET`, Silver `13:24:00-13:25:00 ET`, Platinum `13:03:00-13:05:00 ET`, Copper `12:59:00-13:00:00 ET`, Palladium `12:58:00-13:00:00 ET`, Treasuries `13:59:30-14:00:00 CT`.

**So the envelope alone can never answer the question.** The decision rule that actually worked, and that the next session should apply:

> A trade-type shape earns its own key when **CME states the instant in session language** — "trading halts … daily", "trading ceases daily at", "TAS TRADING HOURS", "TRADING HOURS … BTIC:", a `closed@` event in the trading-hours service, or a stated daily break. It stays UNMAPPED when the only CME statement is a **calculation window** ("the marker is calculated from trade data from 12:34 – 12:35 p.m. London Time") or an **order-entry cutoff**, and the boundary is otherwise feed-only.

The corollary that caught two near-misses: **"Termination of Trading" is expiry, not a daily close.** CME prints it as a distinct row *adjacent to* the hours row on the Japanese equity fact card, the TMAC page and the crypto BTIC FAQ. Reading it as a session boundary is the failure mode that nearly produced six phantom event-contract families.

### 3.2 Trade-type variants that genuinely reuse an underlying's key

**Exactly one, out of ~180 trade-type roots surveyed.**

- **`6EP`** (Euro FX BTIC+) → `globex_fx`. CME states it in words: *"BTIC+ contracts can be traded through the standard CME Globex trading hours of Sunday-Friday 5:00 p.m.-4:00 p.m. CT."* Its plain sibling `6EB` is not, and the same FAQ says why. Requires narrowing the `excludes … BTIC` clause at `futures_profile.rs:168-169` to exclude BTIC while admitting BTIC+.

**Two candidates that looked like reuse and are not:**

- **`AWT`/`BAT`/…/`CCT`** (commodity-index BTIC). The BTIC verdict cited `AW`/`AWT` sharing one exact envelope signature as the proof that a BTIC can ride the underlying's clock. The cash-products challenge falsified it: CME Submission 23-074 tabulates a *BTIC-specific* window for AW (`5:00 pm – 1:30pm CT`) that is not AW's Globex window (`8:15 am – 1:30 pm CT`), and the sibling pair `DRS`/`DRT` sits on 17:00–16:00 vs 17:00–13:30 CT in the same 2026-08-30 file. **The one supposed counterexample in the whole survey collapsed.**
- **`ES1`/`ES2`/`EQ1`** (equity BTIC+/TACO+). Their window *is* the standard 17:00–16:00 CT envelope — but `globex_equity_index` excludes BTIC/TACO products by name, and CME Globex Notice 2021-06-21 says *"all BTIC and TACO products will not be impacted"* by the 2021-06-28 halt removal, so their halt history diverges. Same envelope, different history → **own key**.

### 3.3 Genuinely distinct families

Everything else. In summary form:

| Shape class | Why distinct |
|---|---|
| **Equity/sector/AIR BTIC** (row 2) | Closes 16:00 ET vs the outright's 17:00 ET. CME prints the two lines **adjacent** on its own spec pages: *"CME Globex: Sunday 6:00 p.m. - Friday - 5:00 p.m. ET"* against *"BTIC: Sunday - Friday 6:00 p.m. - 4:00 p.m. ET"* |
| **Credit BTIC** (6 roots) | Same envelope as equity BTIC, different family (CBOT seg-84 Bloomberg credit, `"5:00 p.m. - 3:00 p.m. CT with a 60-minute break"`). One envelope is not one family |
| **Crypto BTIC** ×3 | 24/7 grid **plus** a 5-minute reference-rate stop at 15:00 / 10:00 / 03:00 CT, rolling the trade date at three different city closes. Two of the three anchors survive a DST probe as genuinely non-Chicago |
| **Nikkei vs TOPIX BTIC** | Identical published sentence, **different actual grid** — Nikkei carries a second `Noon – 5:00 p.m. ET` window, TOPIX does not. Two keys |
| **6EB** (FX BTIC) | Standard FX envelope **plus** a 50-minute London-anchored interruption the underlying does not have |
| **All TAS** | Grain TAS closes 13:15 CT vs `globex_grains` 13:20; livestock TAS 13:00 vs 13:05; energy TAS 13:30 vs 16:00; gold TAS 12:30 vs COMEX 16:00; crypto TAS rolls 15:00 CT vs crypto futures 16:00. Every one is an executable-window difference of 5 minutes to 4 hours |
| **All TAM** | Cross-zone by construction: Chicago open, London/Singapore/Shanghai close |
| **TACO, TMAC** | Own published grids (10:00 CT T-1 → 08:30 CT; 18:00 → 16:00 ET), both excluded by name from `globex_equity_index` |
| **The 10 standalone cash families** | Ordinary outright products that merely share the row-1 envelope or a day-session shape; each has its own rulebook chapter, launch date and (for CVB) its own dated divergence from a family it once matched |

**The "it's just derived" objection, and why it does not remove the work.** Every TAS envelope decomposes as *{underlying's open} + {end of that asset class's settlement determination range}*, and the livestock case proves the derivation (TAS inherited the underlying's open change in 2015/2016 and kept the settlement close). A reviewer can fairly say the crate is minting ~13 keys whose content is a formula. The answer is that the crate answers *"is this identity tradeable at instant t"*: at 14:00 CT a `CL` holder is trading and a `CLT` holder is not — group 80:CT is closed 13:30–16:45 CT and then runs a full Pre-Open/Ready cycle, which a fixing inside a session never produces. "Derived" explains why the divergence exists; it does not remove the need to model it.

**What the parent still owes a decision on: granularity.** CME's own TAS eligibility workbook (`/trading/files/tas-tam-eligibility.xlsx`) has exactly six tabs — *Cryptocurrency TAS / Energy TAS / Grain and Oilseed TAS / Livestock TAS / Metals TAS / Treasury TAS* — and its single "Energy TAS" sheet covers `CLT`, `MCT`, `NGT`, `HHT`, `7FT`, `TAS` and `TTS` together. That is one asset class where this handoff proposes three keys (`globex_energy_tas`, `globex_gasoil_tas`, plus an unmapped Dutch TTF). Decide that on family semantics and history, not on the envelope.

## 4. Where a challenge overturned or qualified a verdict

Four of six challenges returned `verdict_holds: false`. All four **kept the verdict's direction** and corrected its findings.

### 4.1 BTIC — overturned on its central claim, direction survives

- **Overturned:** the verdict's thesis sentence — *"on every one of my ten shapes CME lists the BTIC instrument as a separately scheduled Globex product and publishes trading hours for it that DIFFER from the underlying's … That is sourced, not inferred"* — is falsified by one API call. Live ContractSpecs for **EST (7968), IPT (8027), RVT/RSV (7948)** print the *outright* envelope. The verdict recorded as "sourced" three roots on which CME contradicts itself across two of its own channels. → **U-1**.
- **Corrected:** three shapes moved out of "cannot determine" and are now sourced — **row 20 (DRT/GDT/GIT)** via their underlyings' specs (`"BTIC: Sunday - Friday 5:00 p.m. - 1:30 p.m."`), **row 24 (DVT/E3T)** with the zone corrected from CEST to **Europe/London**, **row 31 (FTC)** with the HK anchor now sourced and the FTC page's flat "3:00 a.m. CT" recorded as wrong. **22 of 23** unsourced row-2 roots closed in one channel. **Rows 23/27** split now primary-sourced (Nikkei's midday leg is `Noon to 5:00 p.m. ET`, published; TOPIX demonstrably lacks it) — a quote the verdict already had in its own evidence block, lifted from `cme_nikkei.rs:54`, and did not use. **Crypto BTIC** reshaped from "foreign-city daily session" to "24/7 grid + one 5-min stop".
- **Qualified:** `6EB` — CME calls the Globex interruption a **"trading close"** and the ClearPort one a **"trading halt"**, with different end times. The verdict's flat "it is a halt in CME's language" is half the story.
- **New requirement:** `cme_nikkei.rs:54` currently calls BTIC *"a separately scheduled trade-registration facility rather than a phase of the outright order book"* — **incompatible with authoring seven executable BTIC keys**. Correct it in the same change set; do not cite it as support.

### 4.2 TAS financial/metals — overturned; two UNRESOLVED rows became the best-evidenced in the group

- **Overturned:** blocker #1, *"NO CME-PUBLISHED TAS SESSION WINDOW EXISTS AFTER 2015-03-22, for any product in this group"*, is **false**. The verdict searched the retired `/trading_hours/` pages and the notice channels but never opened the channel the repo already uses for `globex_weather`, `globex_livestock` and `globex_rough_rice`: **CME's server-rendered contract specification pages**, which print the TAS window in the Trading Hours row.
- **Corrected:** **PLT → `globex_platinum_tas`** and **PAT → `globex_palladium_tas`**, both keyed. The palladium spec is the strongest document in the group because it states open, close **and** a daily 60-minute break — a fixing has no break. Gold/silver/copper keep their keys but the stated gap changes: sourced ~2019 → 2021-06, unsourced 2021-07 → today (CME retired the server-rendered pages; the modern pages are client shells fed by the blocked `/CmeWS/`).
- **Reversed on its own reasoning:** the verdict proposed SER-8863's header Effective Date as the *unconditional* anchor for Treasury TAS. The PDF is retrievable (294,279 bytes) and its **body is conditional too**. And the symbol caution points the wrong way — SER-8863 prints **ZFT**, agreeing with the Reference Sheet, so "ZTF" is a Globex-notice-only error; the real inconsistency is **ZNT vs TNT** in SER-8863's own summary table.
- **Struck:** the CME refdata API is **inadmissible** (HTTP 401), not merely untested. Remove it from any "routes worth trying" list.

- **Overturned:** rows **10, 22, 37** are not undeterminable. **NYMEX & COMEX Submission 10-284 / MRAN RA1005-4 (2010-10-07, effective 2010-10-25)** names `CLT`, `BZT`, `BBT`, `HOT`, `RBT`, `NGT`, `NNT`, `7FT` — plus `GCT` and `SIT` — by exact Globex code with per-product times, under a day-level effective date.
